custom-type.description: Singleton row (key '1') holding cursors and run markers for the Gameball jobs. Created automatically on a job's first run - do not create it by hand. Contains no personal data and no secrets, and deliberately carries no retention-days: it is a cursor, not a queue, and losing it would restart every sweep from its install floor.

key-definition.description: Always the literal '1'. This object type holds exactly one row per site; every Gameball job reads and writes that same row.

attribute-definition.description: The install floor for the Gameball Customer Delta job. Seeded automatically to the current time on the job's very first run, during which the job syncs nothing. Profiles last modified before this instant are never swept, which is what keeps the delta job from degenerating into a full backfill of the existing customer base. Backdate it manually only if you deliberately want a bounded catch-up - the per-run call budget still throttles it.

Resume cursor for the PAGED_CUSTOMER_NO strategy only: the last customerNo the job read. The job writes it after every page and again when a run stops part-way through one, so a run that spends its call budget mid-page does not repeat that page on the next run. The literal 0, which is also what an empty value is read as, means start from the beginning of the customer base; the job writes 0 back when it completes a full pass. Unused by the LAST_MODIFIED strategy.

When the Gameball Customer Delta job last finished. Recorded for operator visibility ONLY - it is never used as a query predicate, because the customer search index is asynchronous and a moving watermark used as a filter loses every profile the index had not yet caught up on.

Counters from the last delta run: profiles read, skipped as unchanged, sent, failed (a rejected call, a call that never arrived, or an exception - a run whose every call threw reads failed=N, never skipped=N), skipped by a gating rule, deferred by the rate governor, Gameball calls issued, elapsed milliseconds, and why the run ended (exhausted, call_budget, read_budget, wall_clock, rate_limited, config_error, cursor_stalled, wrapped). Mirrors what the run wrote to the Gameball log.

custom-type.description: Captured right-to-be-forgotten requests. One row per Gameball customer id awaiting deletion, created the moment an SFCC customer is deleted because the id cannot be recovered afterwards. WARNING: this store is NOT free of personal data - the key is the shopper's Gameball customer id, a pseudonymous identifier, which is precisely what an erasure request exists to remove. Retention is therefore days, not months, and no name, email, mobile or address is ever written here. It is single-purpose: nothing but erasure requests may ever be stored in it, and it carries no payload, no event kind and no priority - it is not, and must never become, a general outbound queue.

key-definition.description: The exact customerId value that was sent to Gameball for this shopper, captured before the SFCC profile was destroyed because after deletion it can never be recovered. Also the deterministic dedupe key: enrolling the same shopper twice updates one row instead of creating two.

attribute-definition.description: PENDING - waiting for the Gameball Customer Erasure job. SUCCESS - Gameball confirmed the customer is gone, which includes the case where Gameball had never heard of them. FAILED - every retry was used up, Gameball rejected the request permanently, or the request sat PENDING for more than 7 days without ever reaching Gameball; an operator must resolve this before platform retention removes the row, and the erasure job stays red until they do.

Which path captured this request: DATA_API (an OCAPI/SCAPI Data API customer delete), HELPER_API (merchant code, a DSAR controller or a partner cartridge calling gameballPrivacyApi.requestErasure), or BM_MANUAL (an operator-initiated request through gameballPrivacyApi.requestErasureById). Business Manager customer deletion is NOT hookable in SFCC and never appears here.
When the erasure was first captured. Never overwritten by a repeat request, so this is the true start of the merchant's statutory response clock.

When the erasure job last called Gameball for this request. Empty means the job has not reached it yet. This counts erasure calls only; the identically-named attribute on Order counts order-tracking attempts and the two are unrelated.
When gbStatus became SUCCESS. The purge horizon set by Gameball Erasure Success Retention (Days) is measured from this instant, not from when the request was captured.

How many times Gameball has been called for this request, compared against Gameball Erasure Max Attempts. Deliberately NOT incremented when SFCC itself refused to make the call - an open circuit breaker or the service rate limiter - because a valve the platform closed must not burn the retry budget. The default of 0 applies to rows created after this metadata was imported; code never trusts it and always reads the value as a number defaulting to zero.

Bounded, scrubbed diagnostic for the last attempt: the cartridge's own disposition, the HTTP status, Gameball's error code and Gameball's requestId, which is the token Gameball support asks for. Never the raw response body, never an address, never any other echoed field - a response body can echo submitted data back, and this store exists to hold as little as possible about the shopper being erased.
